nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 3$ and let $F_n$ be the free group on $n$ generators. For every natural number $k$ there is an element of the derived subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ that is not a product of at most $k$ commutators $xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in \operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$. Equivalently, the supremum $k_n$ of the commutator lengths of the elements of the derived subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Commutator length in Aut(Fₙ) is unbounded

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every $n \ge 3$, writing $F_n$ for the free group on $n$ generators, and for every natural number $k$, some element of the derived subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ is not a product of at most $k$ commutators $xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ of elements of $\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$. This is the answer $k_n = \infty$ to Bardakov's question, which asks for the supremum $k_n$ of the commutator lengths of…
nodes.title: Unbounded commutator length in Aut(Fₙ) (Kourovka 14.15)

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has unbounded commutator length when for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$.
nodes.title: Unbounded commutator length

nodes.summary: For a group $G$ with derived subgroup $G'$, the commutator width $w(G')$ is the least positive integer $m$ such that every element of $G'$ is a product of at most $m$ commutators $aba^{-1}b^{-1}$ with $a, b \in G$; it is $0$ when no such $m$ exists.
nodes.title: Commutator width of the derived subgroup

nodes.summary: There is a finitely presented simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 14.13(b) in the affirmative; the Kourovka Archive cites Caprace and Fujiwara.
nodes.title: A finitely presented simple group with unbounded commutator length

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a finitely presented simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 14.13(b) (Bardakov)

nodes.summary: For a group $G$, a natural number $m$ and $g \in G$, $g$ is a product of at most $m$ commutators when there are $k \le m$ and $a_1, b_1, \dots, a_k, b_k \in G$ with $g = [a_1, b_1] \cdots [a_k, b_k]$, where $[a, b] = aba^{-1}b^{-1}$; for $k = 0$ the empty product is the identity.
nodes.title: Products of a bounded number of commutators

nodes.summary: An element $z$ of a group $G$ is a product of at most $n$ commutators when $z = [x_1, y_1] \cdots [x_k, y_k]$ for some $k \le n$ and some $x_1, y_1, \dots, x_k, y_k \in G$, where $[x, y] = x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$; for $k = 0$ the product is the identity.
nodes.title: Products of at most $n$ commutators

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $n$ a natural number. An element $z \in G$ is a product of at most $n$ commutators when there are $m \le n$ and elements $x_1, y_1, \dots, x_m, y_m \in G$ with $z = [x_1, y_1] \cdots [x_m, y_m]$, where $[x, y] = xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$; for $m = 0$ the empty product is the identity.
nodes.title: Products of at most $n$ commutators (Kourovka 14.15)

nodes.summary: For every finite non-abelian group $G$, the commutator width $w(G')$ of its derived subgroup satisfies $w(G')/|G| \le 1/6$, and for the symmetric group $S_3$ equality holds, $w(S_3')/|S_3| = 1/6$; so Kourovka Problem 16.8 has a positive answer.
nodes.title: The maximal commutator width ratio is one sixth

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite non-abelian group $G$ the commutator width $w(G')$ of its derived subgroup $G'$ satisfies $w(G')/|G| \le 1/6$, and that for the symmetric group $S_3$ equality holds: $w(S_3')/|S_3| = 1/6$.
nodes.title: Bardakov's commutator width ratio claim (Kourovka 16.8)

nodes.summary: There is a simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$. This answers Kourovka Problem 14.13(a) in the affirmative; the Kourovka Archive records examples constructed by Barge and Ghys, and finitely generated ones by Muranov.
nodes.title: A simple group with unbounded commutator length

nodes.summary: The statement that there is a simple group $G$ such that for every natural number $n$ some element of the derived subgroup $[G, G]$ is not a product of at most $n$ commutators $x y x^{-1} y^{-1}$ with $x, y \in G$.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 14.13(a) (Bardakov)

not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.
